# Introduction

Vatly is the European merchant of record for AI, software and digital products. It becomes the legal seller on every sale and handles payments, tax and compliance, so you just ship. Sell subscriptions and one-off products through a single API.

To understand what adopting Vatly involves, start with [Build your own integration](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration). Using a specific platform? Find [Lovable payments with Vatly](https://docs.vatly.com/integrations/lovable) and [Bolt payments with Vatly](https://docs.vatly.com/integrations/bolt) under **Integrations**, with platform-specific setup and agent prompts.

::card-group
  :::card
  ---
  icon: i-heroicons:shopping-cart
  title: Hosted Checkouts
  to: https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/checkouts
  ---
  Create hosted checkout sessions with one API call. Support for one-off products and subscription plans with automatic tax calculation.
  :::

  :::card
  ---
  icon: i-heroicons:arrow-path
  title: Subscriptions
  to: https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/subscriptions
  ---
  Full subscription lifecycle management. Handle upgrades, downgrades, proration, trials, and cancellations.
  :::

  :::card
  ---
  icon: i-heroicons:document-text
  title: Orders & Invoices
  to: https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/orders
  ---
  Every payment generates an order with automatic tax calculation and invoicing. Vatly handles EU VAT, US sales tax, and reporting as your Merchant of Record.
  :::

  :::card
  ---
  icon: i-heroicons:bell-alert
  title: Webhooks
  to: https://docs.vatly.com/guides/webhooks
  ---
  Real-time event notifications for checkouts, orders, subscriptions, refunds, and chargebacks.
  :::
::

## Get started in minutes

1. Create a new account at [vatly.com](https://my.vatly.com){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.
2. Grab your API keys from **Developers » API keys**.
3. Connect your Mollie account.
4. Set up your products.
5. Integrate Vatly using one of our [packages](https://docs.vatly.com/packages).

## Going live

Test mode works from the start, so you can build and test your integration right away. Your live keys work once Vatly has approved you and Mollie has verified your business.

- **Product review.** Vatly is the seller on every sale, so it reviews every product before it goes on sale. A review typically takes one to two business days, and you get an email whether or not the product is approved.
- **Mollie verification.** Mollie verifies your business on your own connected Mollie account. Connect the account you already have, or open one in the same flow.
- **Payouts.** Your earnings go to your own Mollie account after a 7-day hold that covers refunds and disputes. See [Payouts & Settlement](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/payouts).

## Next steps

- [Build your own integration](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration): plan what your app needs and brief your developer or agent
- [Quickstart guide](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/quickstart): make your first API call
- [Authentication](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/authentication): learn how API keys work
- [API Reference](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/customers): explore all endpoints
- [PHP SDK](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/php/readme): get the official PHP package
- [Download OpenAPI spec](https://docs.vatly.com/openapi.yaml){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} for code generation and tooling


# Quickstart

::note
Before you can make requests to the Vatly API, you will need to grab your
API key from your dashboard. You find it under 

[Developers » API keys](https://my.vatly.com){rel=""nofollow""}

.
::

This Quickstart covers your first authenticated API request. To understand the full integration before implementing it, start with [Build your own integration](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration). For platform-specific setup, see [Integrations](https://docs.vatly.com/integrations), including Lovable and Bolt.

## Choose your client

Before making your first API request, choose a client. Vatly offers packages for JavaScript / TypeScript, Python, and PHP, with framework integrations for Django and Laravel. See [available packages](https://docs.vatly.com/packages) for installation and language-specific examples. This page demonstrates a first request with cURL or the PHP SDK.

::code-group{sync="client"}
```bash [cURL]
# cURL is most likely already installed on your machine
curl --version
```

```bash [PHP]
# Install the Vatly PHP SDK
composer require vatly/vatly-api-php
```
::

[Check out our list of first-party SDKs](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/sdks)

## Making your first API request

After picking your preferred client, you are ready to make your first call to the Vatly API. Below, you can see how to send a GET request to the Checkouts endpoint to get a list of all your checkouts. In the cURL example, results are limited to ten checkouts, the default page length for each client.

::code-group{sync="client"}
```bash [cURL]
curl -G https://api.vatly.com/v1/checkouts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer test_your_api_key_here" \
  -d limit=10
```

```php [PHP]
$vatly = new Vatly\Api\VatlyApiClient;
$vatly->setApiKey($key);

$vatly->checkouts->page();
```
::

[Read the docs for the Checkouts endpoint](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/checkouts)

## What's next?

Great, you're now set up with an API client and have made your first request to the API. Here are a few links that might be handy as you venture further into the Vatly API:

- [Grab your API key from the Vatly dashboard](https://my.vatly.com){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}
- [Follow the typical selling flow in Vatly](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/selling-workflow)
- [Check out the Checkouts endpoint](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/checkouts)
- [Learn about the different error messages in Vatly](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/errors)


# Payouts & Settlement

## How you get paid

Vatly settles each payment to your connected Mollie account after a 7-day hold by default. Your share is the sale price excluding the customer's tax, minus Vatly's fee. Where VAT applies to your supply to Vatly, it is settled along with it.

In your Mollie account, you can configure payouts to your own bank account or another one. Mollie's payout schedule and payout fees apply from there.

::note
You need a connected Mollie account to receive live payments. Connect it during onboarding in the Vatly dashboard.
::

## The hold period

The hold starts when a payment is paid. Each payment is settled on its own, so a payment made today is settled about a week from now, regardless of when your other payments were made.

The hold gives room to handle refunds, chargebacks and risk checks before money moves to your account. Vatly can apply a longer hold where risk checks require it.

## Follow your settlements in the dashboard

Open **Settlements** in the Vatly dashboard. Payments are grouped into monthly settlement periods. Each period shows its **Payout release status**:

| Line                        | Meaning                                                                                                  |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Released to your account    | Already settled to your Mollie account.                                                                  |
| Scheduled for release       | Still in its hold period. The next release date is shown alongside.                                      |
| Held for settlement         | Could not be released with the payment itself, so it is handled through the period's settlement instead. |
| Charged back before release | Charged back before its hold ended, so it was not released.                                              |

## Test mode

Test-mode payments are settled after a much shorter hold, so you can follow the full flow while you build. No real money moves in test mode.


# Customer Emails

## Vatly sends the billing emails

As Merchant of Record, Vatly is the seller on your customer's invoice. That makes Vatly responsible for the billing communication with your customers, so you don't need to build receipts, payment reminders or refund confirmations yourself.

Vatly sends these emails automatically. Use [webhooks](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/webhooks) to keep your own application in sync, for example to grant or revoke access. Anything about your product itself, such as onboarding or usage emails, stays with you.

## What your customers see

Every customer email:

- Shows your storefront name and logo in the header
- Is sent by Vatly, and states that the sale is made by Vatly
- Points billing and payment questions to [Vatly support](https://vatly.com/support){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}
- Is written in English

Set your storefront name and logo in the Vatly dashboard under **Settings » Branding**. Until you set a name, customers see a placeholder name in their emails.

## Purchases and invoices

| Email        | When it is sent                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Receipt      | After every successful payment: a one-off purchase, the first payment of a subscription, and every renewal. It lists the items, any discount and the VAT, and links to the invoice. |
| Invoice link | When a customer opens an expired invoice link and requests a new one.                                                                                                               |

Each order gets one receipt. The receipt links to the invoice in the customer portal instead of attaching a PDF.

## Subscriptions

| Email                     | When it is sent                                                                                                                                                    |
| ------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Upcoming renewal          | Ahead of the renewal of a subscription billed less often than monthly, or of its first charge after a free trial. It shows the amount, the date and how to cancel. |
| Payment initiated         | When Vatly starts a recurring payment, such as a renewal. It shows the amount, the payment method and the expected charge date.                                    |
| Cancellation confirmation | When the customer cancels their subscription in the customer portal. It confirms until when they keep access.                                                      |
| Cancellation notice       | When you cancel a subscription through the API, or Vatly cancels it on your behalf. It tells the customer when their access ends.                                  |

The upcoming renewal email goes out 7 days ahead for plans billed up to every 3 months, 14 days ahead for plans up to every 6 months, and 30 days ahead for longer plans. Monthly and shorter plans don't get one. If the renewal changes after the email went out, for example because you scheduled a plan change, the customer gets an updated email. If the renewal date changes or the subscription is canceled or paused before the email goes out, Vatly doesn't send it. A changed date gets its own email.

If you end a trial early with an immediate plan change, Vatly charges the first paid cycle on the day of the change, so the customer gets the payment emails that day. A subscription that was canceled during its trial keeps its trial end date.

## Payment methods

| Email                          | When it is sent                                                                                                                                               |
| ------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Card expiring                  | When the card used for a subscription is about to expire. It asks the customer to update their payment method.                                                |
| Recurring payment setup failed | When a recurring payment could not be set up because the customer's first payment never completed. It asks the customer to set up their payment method again. |
| Payment method update link     | When a customer opens an expired payment method update link and requests a new one.                                                                           |

## Failed payments

When a recurring payment fails, Vatly starts a payment recovery process for the subscription. The customer receives:

1. A **Payment failed** email straight away.
2. A series of reminders while Vatly retries the payment. The reminders become more urgent as the process continues, ending with a final notice.
3. If the payment still fails, a **Service canceled** email. Vatly cancels the subscriptions that use the failed payment method.

Payment recovery also starts if a customer updates their payment method while a renewal payment is still processing and that payment then fails. Vatly retries using the updated payment method.

When the payment method can't be charged at all, for example because the card is no longer valid, Vatly does not retry. Instead, the customer receives reminders to update their payment method.

As soon as a retry succeeds or the customer adds a working payment method, the reminders stop and the customer receives the usual receipt.

Follow the process on your side with the `order.payment_failed` and `order.paid` webhooks. See [Handling failed subscription payments](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/webhooks#handling-failed-subscription-payments).

## Refunds

| Email            | When it is sent                                                                                                                 |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Refund processed | When a refund is completed, whether you created it through the API or the dashboard. It lists the refunded items and the total. |

## Customer portal

| Email        | When it is sent                                                            |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Sign-in link | When a customer requests a sign-in link on the customer portal login page. |

[Customer portal sessions](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/customers#create-a-customer-portal-session) created through the API return a URL and do not send an email.

## Test mode

Emails for test mode orders are never delivered to a real inbox. Vatly still renders and saves them, so you can review what your customer would receive. Open an order in the dashboard and find its emails under **Emails**.

## Customization

You can't turn off these emails. Most of them are required for Vatly to bill your customers correctly, such as the receipt and the invoice.

Additional email branding is on the [roadmap](https://roadmap.vatly.com/projects/2-merchant-ui/items/26-email-co-branding){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}. Vote for it to let us know it matters to you.


# Build your own integration

You do not need to build a payment form or your own tax and invoicing workflow to sell with Vatly. Vatly is the European merchant of record for AI, software and digital products: it acts as the legal seller and provides hosted checkout. Your app delivers the product and controls access.

This guide helps you decide what to connect before writing code or asking an agent to implement it. Whether a developer or an AI agent does the work, the responsibilities are the same.

## Choose your starting point

- **Using Lovable or Bolt?** Follow the [Lovable](https://docs.vatly.com/integrations/lovable) or [Bolt](https://docs.vatly.com/integrations/bolt) guide for the setup in your platform and a ready-to-use agent prompt. Find platform-specific instructions under [Integrations](https://docs.vatly.com/integrations).
- **Connecting your own app?** Continue below to plan the integration and choose the right implementation documentation.
- **Ready to make an API request?** The [Quickstart](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/quickstart) covers your first authenticated call. It is a technical first step, not a complete payment integration.

## What Vatly handles, and what stays in your app

| Vatly handles                                                                | Your app handles                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Being the legal seller, including tax and customer invoicing for Vatly sales | Your software or digital product, customer accounts, and support for your product |
| The hosted checkout and payment flow                                         | Your pricing UI and the decision about which products a customer can buy          |
| Billing events, including payments and subscription changes                  | Delivering downloads, activating licenses, or granting and updating access        |
| A hosted customer portal for eligible customers                              | Authenticating the customer and opening their portal session securely             |

Portal access requires an issued invoice. See the [customer portal documentation](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/customerportal). Your existing login and database can remain in place; adding Vatly does not require replacing them.

## What a purchase looks like

1. A customer chooses a product or plan in your app.
2. Your backend checks what that customer can buy and asks Vatly to create a checkout. The API key stays on your server.
3. Your app sends the customer to Vatly's hosted checkout to pay, then shows a return page in your app.
4. Vatly sends a signed notification, called a webhook, to your backend. Your app verifies it before recording the purchase and delivering access.
5. For subscriptions, your app keeps access in step with renewals, cancellations, and other billing changes. Refunds and disputes also need an access policy.

The return page is not proof of payment. A customer may close the checkout tab or visit the return URL directly; delivery must depend on the verified billing result, not that browser visit. The [Selling Workflow](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/selling-workflow) walks through the sale lifecycle in more detail.

## Prepare a test integration

[Create a Vatly account](https://my.vatly.com){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}, get a `test_` key under **Developers » API keys**, and create a test product under **Manage Products**. Choose a one-off product for a single purchase or a subscription plan for recurring access. Keep the key, products, and customers in the same storefront and mode.

Your app needs a deployed backend that can call Vatly privately, receive HTTPS webhooks, and store billing state. A frontend-only site needs a backend or server functions for these tasks. Store API keys and webhook signing secrets in that backend's secret manager—not browser code, frontend environment variables, or agent chat.

Test mode is available before going live. Your first milestone is one complete test purchase that grants the right customer access, not a finished billing dashboard.

## Choose your tools

For app-level billing, start with a fluent package rather than assembling every flow from low-level API calls:

- **JavaScript / TypeScript:** [`@getvatly/fluent`](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/readme) builds on `@getvatly/sdk` with checkout and subscription builders, customer bindings, and webhook processing. Follow [configuration](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/configuration) for compatible versions and runtime requirements.
- **PHP:** [PHP Fluent](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-php/webhook-flow) provides higher-level billing flows. The [Laravel package](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/laravel/readme) wires fluent for Laravel.
- **Python:** [Python Fluent](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-python/readme) provides async-first billing flows and storage contracts. The [Django package](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/django/readme) integrates fluent with Django's ORM and webhook handling. Both are available on PyPI.
- **Direct API access:** Use the matching [SDK](https://docs.vatly.com/packages) when you only need the API client, or the [HTTP API](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference) from another server-side language. The [Python SDK](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/python/readme) is available on PyPI as `vatly-api-python` (import `vatly`).

The JavaScript, Python, Django and PHP fluent packages are **alpha**. Every alpha release may include breaking changes. Pin exact versions during alpha. Follow each package's installation guidance and review upgrades. Fluent packages provide building blocks, not your app's access policy or a database integration that configures itself: your developer or agent must wire the required storage drivers and authorization checks.

## Hand off a clear brief

Give your developer or agent the decisions that belong to your business:

- Which products or plans you will sell, and what each purchase unlocks.
- Which existing login, database, and deployed backend to use.
- Where customers should return after completing or canceling checkout.
- How access should change after a renewal, cancellation, refund, or dispute.

Ask them to follow the chosen package's checkout and webhook documentation, and to show you the deployed checkout flow and webhook URL. Secrets should be entered through the host's secure secret form, never included in the brief. Agents can use the [documentation index](https://docs.vatly.com/llms.txt){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}, [API reference](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference), and [OpenAPI specification](https://docs.vatly.com/openapi.yaml){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} to check implementation details.

## Know when you are ready to sell

Before switching to live credentials, review the integration as a customer:

- A completed test purchase grants the right access; a canceled checkout or a visit to the return URL alone does not.
- Customers cannot buy on another user's account or grant themselves access through the browser.
- Repeated webhook deliveries do not fulfill a purchase twice, invalid signatures are rejected, and failed processing can retry.
- Subscription and post-payment changes follow the access policy you chose.

Your implementer can use the [webhook guide](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/webhooks), [test-mode guide](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/testing), and package-specific tests for these checks. Live selling also requires [Vatly approval, product review, and Mollie verification](https://docs.vatly.com/introduction#going-live). A working test integration is not a guarantee of a go-live date.


# Selling Workflow

Planning your integration? Start with [Build your own integration](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration) for responsibilities, implementation choices, and a brief for your developer or agent. This page follows the sale itself, from setup through delivery and post-payment events.

## The typical Vatly flow

For most use cases, the Vatly integration follows the same happy path:

1. Create your Vatly account and collect your API key.
2. Configure the products you want to sell in the Vatly dashboard.
3. Register a webhook endpoint that Vatly can reach.
4. Create a checkout with the product IDs you want to sell.
5. Redirect the customer to the hosted checkout URL.
6. Listen for the payment webhook and fulfill the order in your app.
7. Stay prepared to handle refunds and chargebacks after the sale.

This guide ties those steps together so you can see the full flow before diving into each API endpoint.

## 1. Finish the initial setup

Start with the basics:

- Create your Vatly account.
- Grab your API keys from the dashboard under **Developers » API keys**.
- For live payments, connect your Mollie account and complete onboarding with both Mollie and Vatly.

Most merchants and developers should begin in test mode. In test mode, the customers, products, and checkouts you create stay in your test environment so you can validate the full flow safely before you start accepting real payments. The online Vatly dashboard has a testmode toggle. For API calls, use your dedicated test API key (starting with `test_`).

When you are ready to sell for real, switch to live mode. Each product you want to sell must be verified by Vatly before it can be used in a live selling flow.

Do not wait until the last minute to create your products in the dashboard. Product verification can take some time because Vatly needs to review them for compliance before they can be used in a live selling flow.

If you have not made your first authenticated request yet, start with the [Quickstart guide](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/quickstart).

## 2. Set up the products you want to sell

Before you can create a checkout, you need at least one product in Vatly.

You can sell two kinds of products:

- [One-off products](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/one-off-products) for a single purchase such as a digital download, license, or one-time service.
- [Subscription plans](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/subscription-plans) for recurring access such as a SaaS plan.

Products are configured in the Vatly dashboard. After creating them, keep track of their product IDs because you will need those IDs when you create a checkout through the API.

## 3. Register your webhook before going live

Set up your webhook endpoint before you send customers to checkout. That endpoint is how Vatly tells your application that something important happened, such as a checkout being paid, a subscription changing, or a refund being created.

Configure the webhook in the dashboard and make sure the endpoint is:

- Reachable from the public internet
- Served over HTTPS
- Able to verify the `Vatly-Signature` header

This is a critical part of the integration. Use webhooks to confirm what happened instead of relying only on the customer's browser returning to your site.

[Read the webhook guide](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/webhooks)

## 4. Create a checkout for the right products

When a customer is ready to buy, your app creates a checkout with the product IDs you configured earlier. A checkout can contain:

- A single one-off product
- A single subscription plan
- A list of products, depending on what your flow allows

The API request is made from your backend using your secret API key.

::code-group
```bash [cURL]
curl https://api.vatly.com/v1/checkouts \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer live_your_api_key_here" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "products": [
      { "id": "one_off_product_Vr8kQdFhSrG4Y3DnfsdqH", "quantity": 1 }
    ],
    "redirectUrlSuccess": "https://example.com/success",
    "redirectUrlCanceled": "https://example.com/canceled"
  }'
```

```php [PHP]
use Vatly\Api\VatlyApiClient;

$vatly = new VatlyApiClient();
$vatly->setApiKey('live_your_api_key_here');

$checkout = $vatly->checkouts->create([
    'products' => [
        [
            'id' => 'one_off_product_Vr8kQdFhSrG4Y3DnfsdqH',
            'quantity' => 1,
        ],
    ],
    'redirectUrlSuccess' => 'https://example.com/success',
    'redirectUrlCanceled' => 'https://example.com/canceled',
]);

$checkoutUrl = $checkout->links->checkoutUrl->href;

return redirect()->away($checkoutUrl);
```
::

The response includes a hosted checkout URL in `links.checkoutUrl.href`. That is the URL your customer should visit to complete payment.

```json [Response]
{
  "id": "checkout_QGQ0qDrQ2B4O1yXVTr6Wc",
  "status": "created",
  "redirectUrlSuccess": "https://example.com/success",
  "redirectUrlCanceled": "https://example.com/canceled",
  "links": {
    "checkoutUrl": {
      "href": "https://checkout.vatly.com/chk_test_123456789"
    }
  }
}
```

[Read the Checkouts API reference](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/checkouts)

## 5. Redirect the customer to the checkout URL

After creating the checkout, redirect the customer to the URL returned by Vatly.

At that point, Vatly handles the hosted payment flow. The customer completes payment on the Vatly checkout page and is then redirected back to your success or cancellation URL.

The browser redirect is helpful for user experience, but your backend should still wait for the relevant webhook event before treating the order as paid.

## 6. Fulfill the order after payment

Once the checkout is paid, Vatly notifies your webhook endpoint. That is the point where your application should decide what to deliver.

Typical fulfillment actions include:

- Granting access to your SaaS
- Sending an email with access instructions
- Providing a download link for a digital product
- Activating a subscription in your own application

The exact webhook event you handle depends on your setup, but `checkout.paid` and the related order or subscription events are the key signals that the sale completed.

## 7. Prepare for post-payment events

The happy path ends with a successful sale and fulfillment, but a production integration also needs to handle post-payment scenarios.

At minimum, merchants and developers should be prepared for:

- [Refunds](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/refunds), whether partial or full
- [Chargebacks](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/chargebacks), which are created when a payment dispute is initiated

These events should also flow through your webhook handling so your application can revoke access, update account state, notify staff, or trigger follow-up support processes when needed.

Vatly actively prevents and disputes chargebacks. If extra evidence is needed, Vatly will check in with you for details such as proof of delivery or proof that the customer received access to the product.

## Where to go next

- [Quickstart](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/quickstart)
- [Webhooks](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/webhooks)
- [Checkouts API](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/checkouts)
- [One-off Products API](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/one-off-products)
- [Subscription Plans API](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/subscription-plans)
- [Refunds API](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/refunds)
- [Chargebacks API](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/chargebacks)


# Vatly SDKs

Vatly is the European merchant of record for AI, software and digital products. Use a fluent package for app-level billing, or an SDK for direct API calls.

## PHP SDK

The official PHP SDK is the primary way to interact with the Vatly API from your PHP application.

For installation, usage examples, and the full list of available resources, see the [PHP SDK docs](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/php/readme).

## PHP Fluent

[`vatly/vatly-fluent-php`](https://packagist.org/packages/vatly/vatly-fluent-php){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} adds higher-level billing flows to the PHP SDK.

```bash
composer require vatly/vatly-fluent-php
```

Follow its [README](https://github.com/vatly/vatly-fluent-php#readme){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} for setup. The synced docs currently cover [webhook flow](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-php/webhook-flow) and [adapting to your framework](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-php/host-owns-its-tables).

## Laravel

The Vatly Laravel package was inspired by Laravel Cashier and provides a fluent way of integrating Vatly into your application.

For installation and usage examples, see the [Laravel Vatly docs](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/laravel/readme).

## JavaScript SDK

The official JavaScript / TypeScript SDK, [`@getvatly/sdk`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@getvatly/sdk){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}, provides a typed client for the Vatly API on Node.js and edge runtimes.

```bash
npm install @getvatly/sdk
```

For installation, usage examples, and the full list of available resources, see the [JavaScript / TypeScript SDK docs](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/javascript/readme). The source is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/vatly/vatly-api-js){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

## JavaScript Fluent

The framework-agnostic fluent package, [`@getvatly/fluent`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@getvatly/fluent){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}, builds on `@getvatly/sdk` with checkout builders, customer and subscription handles, and webhook processing.

```bash
npm install @getvatly/sdk @getvatly/fluent
```

For installation and usage examples, see the [fluent JavaScript / TypeScript docs](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/readme). The source is available on [GitHub](https://github.com/vatly/vatly-fluent-js){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

## Python SDK

[`vatly-api-python`](https://pypi.org/project/vatly-api-python/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} provides typed synchronous and asynchronous API clients for Python 3.10+. Import it as `vatly`.

```bash
pip install vatly-api-python
```

See the [Python SDK docs](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/python/readme) for initialization and API resources, or the source on [GitHub](https://github.com/vatly/vatly-api-python){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

## Python Fluent

[`vatly-fluent-python`](https://pypi.org/project/vatly-fluent-python/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} builds on the Python SDK with async-first billing flows, checkout builders, subscriptions and transactional webhooks. Import it as `vatly_fluent`.

```bash
pip install vatly-fluent-python
```

See the [Python Fluent docs](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-python/readme) for storage contracts and configuration, or the source on [GitHub](https://github.com/vatly/vatly-fluent-python){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

## Django

[`vatly-django`](https://pypi.org/project/vatly-django/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} integrates Python Fluent with Django, including ORM storage, billable operations and webhook handling. Import it as `vatly_django`.

```bash
pip install vatly-django
```

See the [Django docs](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/django/readme) for installation and settings, or the source on [GitHub](https://github.com/vatly/vatly-django){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}. Like Laravel for PHP, Django is the framework integration; its reference lives under Packages.

These packages are in alpha. Every alpha release may include breaking changes. Pin exact versions during alpha. All three Python packages are released at `0.1.0a2`; for example, use `pip install vatly-django==0.1.0a2` to pin Django and its matching Python package dependencies.

---

In the meantime, you can use the [REST API directly](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/authentication) with any HTTP client in any language.
