Connect Fluent to your existing tables through storage drivers. Your application
owns the database, authentication, and jobs; Fluent supplies the contracts.

```ts
import type { Order } from '@getvatly/sdk';
import type { LocalSubscription, Repository, Stored, Wiring } from '@getvatly/fluent';

export function storageDrivers(
  subscriptions: Repository<LocalSubscription>,
  orders: Repository<Stored<Order>>,
): Pick<Wiring, 'subscriptions' | 'orders'> {
  return { subscriptions, orders };
}
```

## Repository behavior

`Stored<T>` adds `hostCustomerId` to the SDK resource. It is null for an unattributed
customer. `LocalSubscription` also adds `endsAt`.

| Method                | Return value                                                                             |
| --------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `findByVatlyId(id)`   | Record or null.                                                                          |
| `store(data)`         | Saved record, or null to decline storage and skip the local-created event.               |
| `update(id, partial)` | Updated record. Omitted/`undefined` fields stay unchanged; null clears a nullable field. |

Enforce unique Vatly IDs per tenant, storefront, and mode. Adapt existing tables
rather than duplicating them. `store` can match a pending host record using
checkout metadata and attach its Vatly ID. Metadata helps match records; it does
not authorize access.

`refunds` and `chargebacks` use `ReversalRepository`, which adds `listForOrder(id)`
and `listForCustomer(id)`. Contracts accept sync or async implementations, except
`webhookCalls.process`, which returns a promise.

## Billables and bindings

Keep your user, team, or organization as the billable; there is no `Billable` mixin.
`CustomerProfile` carries `vatlyId`, `email`, and optional `name`. Your application's
ID (`hostId`) is separate from Vatly's customer ID (`vatlyId`). Authorize both.

| `CustomerBindings` method    | Behavior                                                              |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `bind(vatlyId, hostId)`      | Associate IDs atomically; enforce uniqueness on both sides.           |
| `record(vatlyId)`            | Record an unattributed customer without clearing an existing binding. |
| `vatlyCustomerIdFor(hostId)` | Return the Vatly ID or null.                                          |
| `hostCustomerIdFor(vatlyId)` | Return the host ID or null.                                           |

Do not silently reassign bindings. Keep test and live data separate. See
[customers](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/customers) for creation and lookup examples.

## Webhook storage

Wire `webhookCalls` for deduplication and audit retention, and `events` for outbox
writes. They must share a transaction with repositories and bindings. Use your
database's transaction context or request-scoped drivers, not a global variable
shared by concurrent requests. The [webhook transaction steps](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/webhooks#idempotency-and-one-transaction)
define what must commit or roll back together.

For remote resource fields, use the [API reference](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.


# Customer portal

Send a signed-in customer to their invoices and subscription controls:

```ts
import type { Vatly } from '@getvatly/fluent';

export async function portalUrl(vatly: Vatly, authenticatedHostId: string) {
  const customer = await vatly.customers.findByHostCustomerId(authenticatedHostId);
  if (!customer) return null;
  const session = await vatly.customer(customer.id).portalSession({
    returnUrl: 'https://app.example.com/account/billing',
  });
  return session.url;
}
```

Look up the customer through [bindings](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/customers); do not accept a customer ID
from the browser. Redirect to the returned URL with `Cache-Control: no-store`.
It is a short-lived, single-use credential: never log, cache, or persist it. If an
idempotent retry returns a consumed link, request another with a fresh key.

An eligible issued invoice is required; a subscription alone is not enough.
One-off buyers can view invoice history too. On an eligibility 404, show your
billing page instead of retrying.

The portal stays in the key's storefront and mode, with no storefront picker.
`returnUrl` is an HTTPS return link, not an automatic redirect. For a direct
billing-details flow, see [subscriptions](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/subscriptions#update-billing-details).

For eligibility and response fields, see
[Create a customer portal session](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/customers#create-a-customer-portal-session){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.


# Testing

Test API calls without a network by injecting the SDK's `fetch`:

```ts
import { VatlyClient } from '@getvatly/sdk';
import { Vatly } from '@getvatly/fluent';

export async function testCheckoutLookup() {
  const vatly = new Vatly({
    api: new VatlyClient({
      apiKey: 'test_local_fixture_not_a_real_key',
      maxRetries: 0,
      fetch: async (input, init) => {
        if (new URL(String(input)).pathname !== '/v1/checkouts/checkout_fixture'
          || init?.method !== 'GET') throw new Error('Unexpected request');
        return new Response(JSON.stringify({ customerId: 'customer_fixture' }), {
          headers: { 'content-type': 'application/json' },
        });
      },
    }),
  });
  const id = await vatly.customerIdFromCheckout('checkout_fixture');
  if (id !== 'customer_fixture') throw new Error('Incorrect customer');
}
```

This fixture tests only customer lookup. Use full resource fixtures for other
operations; SDK types do not validate them at runtime.

## Test your storage boundary

Check the [storage contracts](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/coreconcepts): uniqueness under concurrency,
test/live separation, omitted versus null updates, and a declined `store`.

For [webhooks](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/webhooks), test valid, invalid, stale, and rotated signatures
using an independent HMAC signer. Concurrent copies must commit once. A failed
reaction must roll back rows, audit markers, and outbox work, then succeed on retry.
Also test unknown events and out-of-order snapshots. Keep timestamp checks enabled.

## Live test-mode workflow

1. Set `VATLY_API_KEY` to a real `test_` key. Use customer and catalogue IDs from
   its storefront and mode. Test keys do not create real charges.
2. Expose your local webhook route through an HTTPS tunnel. Register the public
   URL and save its signing secret as `VATLY_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
3. Pay through a [hosted checkout](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/checkouts). Save the checkout/order IDs and
   confirm signed `checkout.paid` and `order.paid` deliveries.
4. Check duplicate and failed deliveries. Delete or disable temporary endpoints
   before closing the tunnel; record any resources you create.

`vatly.testHelpers()` exposes `advanceRenewal`, `forceRenewalPaid`,
`forceRenewalFailed`, `forceOrderPaymentPaid`, `forceOrderPaymentFailed`, and the
SDK-style `fastForwardRenewal`/`simulateOrderPayment`. These mutate account data.
Use them only with permission and disposable test resources, not existing
subscriptions or orders just because the key is in test mode.

## Test your edge runtime

For edge hosts, also run your app in the local edge runtime with its storage adapter.
Node tests alone do not check edge compatibility.

See the [testing guide](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/testing){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} and
[Test Helpers API reference](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/test-helpers){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.


# Getting started

> **Alpha — under active development. Every alpha release may include breaking changes. Pin exact versions during alpha.**

Use `vatly-api-python==0.1.0a2`, imported as `vatly`. Requires Python 3.10+.
Create `VatlyClient` inside `with`, or `AsyncVatlyClient` inside `async with`, to
close the connection pool. Both accept an explicit API key or `VATLY_API_KEY`.
Test and live modes use the same API host; keys select the mode.

See the [SDK README](https://github.com/vatly/vatly-api-python/blob/main/README.md){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} for runnable initialization, checkout,
pagination, retries, configuration, errors and development commands.

# Customers

`client.customers` provides `create`, `get`, `update`, `list`, `list_all`,
`create_portal_session`, `list_subscriptions`, `list_all_subscriptions`, and
`get_subscription`. Filter by email via `ListCustomersParams(email=...)` or
`{"email": "person@example.com"}`. Email identity is storefront- and mode-scoped.

`update` changes identity name/email, not billing-address details. Portal sessions
are short-lived and single-use: redirect to the returned `url`; do not store it as
a permanent link. Pass `{}` for an empty portal-session request body.

See [method inventory](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/python/api#customers) and [customer fields](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/customers){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.


# API reference

Generated from `openapi.yaml`. Sync and async clients expose the same methods.
Pass a Pydantic request/params model or a wire-format dictionary. All methods accept keyword-only `options=RequestOptions(...)`.

## `checkouts`

| Method              | HTTP endpoint                 | Returns          |
| ------------------- | ----------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `list(params=None)` | `GET /checkouts`              | `Page[Checkout]` |
| `create(body)`      | `POST /checkouts`             | `Checkout`       |
| `get(checkout_id)`  | `GET /checkouts/{checkoutId}` | `Checkout`       |

## `customers`

| Method                                           | HTTP endpoint                                                | Returns              |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------- |
| `list(params=None)`                              | `GET /customers`                                             | `Page[Customer]`     |
| `create(body)`                                   | `POST /customers`                                            | `Customer`           |
| `get(customer_id)`                               | `GET /customers/{customerId}`                                | `Customer`           |
| `update(customer_id, body)`                      | `PATCH /customers/{customerId}`                              | `Customer`           |
| `create_portal_session(customer_id, body)`       | `POST /customers/{customerId}/portal-sessions`               | `PortalSession`      |
| `list_subscriptions(customer_id, params=None)`   | `GET /customers/{customerId}/subscriptions`                  | `Page[Subscription]` |

# Checkouts

Use `client.checkouts.create(CreateCheckoutRequest(...))` to create a hosted payment
page. Redirect to `checkout.links.checkout_url.href`. Products use Vatly product
IDs and quantities. Both success/cancellation redirect URLs are required. Use
`customer_id` for an existing authorized customer, or omit it for an anonymous flow.

Read one checkout with `get(id)`, one page with `list(params)`, or iterate with
`list_all(params)`. Async clients use `await` and `async for` respectively.
Reuse a business-operation idempotency key across caller retries. Confirm payment
through signed webhooks, not a browser redirect. A checkout's `order_id` links to
the order; the checkout itself intentionally has no products array.

See [method inventory](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/python/api#checkouts) and [production checkout fields](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/checkouts){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.


# Subscriptions

Use `client.subscriptions.get(id)`, `list(params)`, or `list_all(params)` to read.
Create a subscription through a checkout containing a subscription-plan ID.

`update(id, body)` changes plan, price or quantity. At least one is required;
`trial_until` cannot be sent alone. By default updates are scheduled; request
`apply_immediately` and the relevant invoice/proration flags deliberately.
`cancel(id, {"immediately": True})` encodes the boolean as `1`, as the server expects.
`resume(id)` is only valid during the cancellation grace period.

`create_billing_update_link(id, body)` returns a hosted link for billing details;
both redirect URLs are required. Check remote status before granting entitlements.
The signed subscription events carry full snapshots, including scheduled changes,
mandate, cancellation reason, and renewal periods.

Test-only helpers live under `client.test_helpers`: `fast_forward_renewal` and
`simulate_order_payment`. They mutate remote data and must never run in CI/live
verification without explicit intent. This repository's tests use mocks only.

See [method inventory](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/python/api#subscriptions) and [subscription fields](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/subscriptions){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.


# Subscription plans

`client.subscription_plans` provides `list`, `list_all`, `get`, `create`, `update`,
`archive`, and `unarchive`. Use `CreateSubscriptionPlanRequest` and
`UpdateSubscriptionPlanRequest` from `vatly.models`. Money is a decimal string
plus currency; preserve both. Archiving returns `None`, unarchiving the plan.

Test-mode product changes are auto-approved; live changes may await approval.
Archive prevents new sales, not existing subscription renewals. Select
`includeArchived` in dictionary filters when needed, or the corresponding model's
`include_archived` field.

See [method inventory](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/python/api#subscription_plans) and [plan fields](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/subscription-plans){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.


# Orders

`client.orders` provides read/pagination plus nested refunds and chargebacks.
`create_invoice_update_link(order_id)` returns a hosted billing-details update
link. Financial money values remain decimal strings. Tax and metadata fields are
retained; do not reconstruct invoices from rounded float calculations.

An order line's `product_type` selects what `product_id` refers to. Readers must
support `subscription_plan` lines (plan IDs) and `subscription` lines
(subscription IDs). This alpha has no typed related-resources accessor;
extra output fields are preserved. Do not assume a plan reference identifies
the customer's subscription.
Never grant access from an ID alone; verify ownership and subscription status.

See [method inventory](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/python/api#orders) and [order fields](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/orders){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.


# Refunds

Read refunds via `client.refunds.list`, `list_all`, and `get`. Order-scoped
operations are `orders.list_refunds`, `list_all_refunds`, `get_refund`,
`create_refund`, `create_full_refund`, and `cancel_refund`.

Partial refunds use `CreateRefundRequest` with order lines and amounts; full
refunds accept `CreateFullRefundRequest` or `{}`. A cancellation returns `None`.
Use stable idempotency keys for business operations; a timeout does not prove
that a refund failed. Read/reconcile before issuing another mutation when the
server reports an unknown outcome. Webhooks confirm completion/failure/cancellation.

See [method inventory](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/python/api#refunds) and [refund fields](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/refunds){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.


# One-off products

`client.one_off_products` provides `list`, `list_all`, `get`, `create`, `update`,
`archive`, and `unarchive`. Use `CreateOneOffProductRequest` and
`UpdateOneOffProductRequest` from `vatly.models`. `archive` returns `None`;
`unarchive` returns the resource. Mode and approval behavior follow the API key.

The output `product_type` preserves product type strings not yet listed in the
production spec (including observed `digital_download`). Request validation still
follows the production request schema. Unknown response fields are preserved.

See [method inventory](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/python/api#one_off_products) and [product fields](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/one-off-products){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.


# Chargebacks

Read disputes via `client.chargebacks.list`, `list_all`, and `get`, or the
order-scoped `orders.list_chargebacks`, `list_all_chargebacks`, and `get_chargeback`.
All are read-only. Preserve the signed financial snapshot for accounting.

`order.chargeback_received` and `order.chargeback_reversed` webhook deliveries
carry a Chargeback in `object` even though `entity_type` is `order`.
Use `object.resource`, not the envelope entity type, to inspect the resource.

See [method inventory](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/python/api#chargebacks) and [chargeback fields](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/chargebacks){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.


# Webhooks

> Alpha — under active development. Every alpha release may include breaking changes. Pin exact versions during alpha.

Verify the exact raw request bytes before parsing or acting. This example is
framework-independent; obtain `raw_body` and the signature header in your server:

```python
from vatly.webhooks import construct_webhook_event


def receive(raw_body: bytes, signature: str, secret: str):
    event = construct_webhook_event(raw_body, signature, secret)
    if not event.known:
        return retain_for_triage(event)  # your durable storage
    return handle_verified_event(event)  # your application
```

Header: `Vatly-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256>`.
Signed input: timestamp, a period, then raw body. Default absolute clock-skew
tolerance is 300 seconds, including future timestamps. Zero disables freshness.
Secret sequences support rotation. Unknown signature versions are ignored.
`verify_webhook_signature` raises `VatlyInvalidSignatureError`; the boolean helper
is `is_valid_webhook_signature`. `construct_event` returns the strict production
`WebhookDelivery`. `construct_webhook_event` additionally supports future event
names with `known=False`, preserving their payload. Known objects are Pydantic
resources discriminated by `object.resource`, not `entityType`: chargeback events
have an order entity but a chargeback object. Setup events need no links.

Timestamp checks are not deduplication. Deduplicate by the &#x2A;*signed `event.id`**
in the same transaction as business changes and your outbox. The header
`Vatly-Event-Id` is useful for diagnostics but is not the signed authority.
Return success only after committing; let storage/processing failures retry.
No framework adapters, persistence, or implicit API reads are installed by the SDK.


# Development and release

## Sources

`openapi.yaml` was fetched on 2026-11-09 from <https://docs.vatly.com/openapi.yaml>{rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"},
byte-identical to `vatly/vatly-docs/public/openapi.yaml` at
`7e71ade32d311b10f79e10c15d0ac03ae32bde97`.
SHA-256: `69640ac82bbba8d101e6aa882facd5f13aa5cf67f38508e5cea18abef03c4940`.
The spec's generated-at date is not the retrieval date.
JS design reference: `vatly/vatly-api-js` at `8b0b920c29f7e7b30bf71b9e379ec0a8a1a22028`.

To update, deliberately replace the pinned spec from that production URL, update
this provenance, run `uv run python scripts/generate.py`, inspect the diff, and
run all README checks. CI checks regeneration offline. Do not edit generated files.

Output objects preserve extra fields. URLs/emails remain strings. Input enums
and constraints are generated from the spec. Two observed production differences
are handled explicitly: empty metadata `[]` normalizes to `{}`, and the output
OneOffProduct.productType is an open string (production returns `digital_download`).
The checked-in spec is not patched. Response validation failures surface as
`VatlyApiError` with the Pydantic cause; response bodies may contain personal data.
Do not log them indiscriminately.

## Documentation sync

`docs/README.md`, `API.md`, and the resource guides mirror the JS SDK's layout.
Pushes to `main` affecting `docs/**` notify `vatly/vatly-docs`, which imports
these guides automatically. The notifier requires the Actions secret
`VATLY_DOCS_DISPATCH_TOKEN` with Contents: write access to `vatly/vatly-docs`.
Keep relative links portable.
`API.md` is generated; prose guides are maintained manually.

## Orb setup

`.agents/setup` is executable, provisions uv 0.12.9 and Python 3.12, syncs the
lockfile, and checks imports. It does not read API credentials or make API calls.
Run twice to check warm behavior. No services or resume repairs are needed.
It will become available to project orbs once pushed to the default branch and
the repository is connected as an Amp project.

## PyPI releases

[`vatly-api-python` 0.1.0a2](https://pypi.org/project/vatly-api-python/0.1.0a2/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}
was published on 2026-11-12. The import name remains `vatly`.

1. Push reviewed code to the public `vatly/vatly-api-python` repository's main branch.
2. Keep the PyPI trusted publisher for project `vatly-api-python`, owner `vatly`,
   repository `vatly-api-python`, workflow `release.yml`; leave the environment field blank.
   No GitHub environment or PyPI token is needed.
3. Update both package-version sources and changelog, run CI, and only with approval
   create a new `v<version>` tag and publish its GitHub release (mark alphas as prereleases).
   Never reuse a published version or move an existing release tag.
4. The release workflow validates/builds first, then exchanges GitHub OIDC for PyPI
   credentials. Anyone able to publish a matching GitHub release can initiate publication;
   restrict repository release access accordingly. Publish the SDK before Fluent.

**A private GitHub repository does not make PyPI artifacts private.** Publishing
uploads the wheel and sdist publicly, including their source and packaged docs.


# Getting started

> **Alpha — under active development. Every alpha release may include breaking changes. Pin exact versions during alpha.**

Use Fluent for a billing integration; use the raw SDK for direct API calls. Fluent
depends on `vatly-api-python==0.1.0a2` and Python 3.10+. Follow the [quick start](https://github.com/vatly/vatly-fluent-python/blob/main/README.md){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}
for your first hosted checkout, then add storage for signed events and ownership.

Pushes to `main` affecting `docs/**` notify `vatly/vatly-docs`, which imports
these guides automatically. The notifier requires the Actions secret
`VATLY_DOCS_DISPATCH_TOKEN` with Contents: write access to `vatly/vatly-docs`.


# Customers

Use `customers.create_for(host_id, CustomerProfile(email=..., name=...))` with
bindings, or `create_unattributed(profile)` to record billing identity without a
host binding. `attribute(vatly_id, host_id)` checks both sides and delegates atomic
uniqueness to the driver. It never reassigns identities. Reuse an explicit
idempotency key when retrying creation after a local binding failure.

Look up by `find_by_host_customer_id`, `find_by_vatly_customer_id`,
`find_one_by_email`, or iterate `find_by_email`. Email is storefront/mode scoped,
not a global customer key. All host/customer IDs require server authorization.

`vatly.customer(id)` memoizes its full SDK resource via `await handle.model()`.
`name`, `email` and `identity` share the cache; `sync()` refreshes it and `update`
refreshes from the mutation response. Updating name/email changes communication
identity, not invoice billing details. Use the hosted portal/billing flows instead.

`customer_id_from_checkout(id)` returns billing identity only.
`claim_customer_from_checkout(id, host_id)` requires host-verified checkout ownership
and only binds the customer; neither method assigns order/subscription entitlements.
Resource ownership follows the host's checkout records, never customerId.


# Checkouts

`vatly.checkout_builder(profile)` handles one-off and mixed carts. Call
`.with_items([{"id": product_id, "quantity": 2}])`; repeated calls append detached
copies. `vatly.subscribe(profile).to_plan(plan_id).with_quantity(3)` creates a
single-plan checkout builder. Trial methods are `with_trial_days` and
`with_trial_ends_at(aware_datetime)`, rounded up to whole days. Quantity and trial
days must be positive integers. No request occurs until `await builder.create()`.

Both builders offer `with_redirect_url_success`, `with_redirect_url_canceled`,
`with_locale`, `with_metadata`, `with_billing_address`, `in_testmode`, and
`in_live_mode`. Mode methods assert the key's mode; they cannot change it.
`payload(overrides)` returns a deep detached wire-format dictionary.
`create(overrides, options=RequestOptions(...))` returns a full SDK Checkout plus
`get_url()`. Subscription builders replace rather than accumulate their plan item.

Use `.for_entity(EntityRef("team", authorized_team_id))` with `checkouts` wiring to
save ownership locally. A profile's `vatly_id` selects billing identity, not entity
ownership. Authorize all overrides on the server. Persist a purchase ID before
calling the API and reuse its idempotency key if the API or local save times out.
If local persistence fails after the API succeeds, retry with that **same key**.
Never blindly issue a second purchase. SDK auto-keys cover internal retries only.

Checkout redirects do not prove payment. Use signed events and reconciliation.
Checkout objects stay lean: read lines from checkout.order\_id's Order, not from
invented checkout.products fields. [Subscriptions](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-python/subscriptions) covers old
plan references and the pending core order-line change.


# Subscriptions

Authorize a `LocalSubscription` from your repository, then call
`vatly.subscription(local)`. `swap(plan_id, body)` defaults to scheduled changes;
`swap_and_invoice` forces immediate application/invoicing; `swap_without_charge`
forces immediate application and disables the proration charge. Local data follows
the API response, so a scheduled swap does not prematurely replace the active plan.

`cancel(immediately=True)` sends the API mutation and waits for signed events to
update local cancellation state. `resume()` clears local `ends_at` after API success.
`sync()` saves the complete snapshot and derives expiry through `subscription_ends_at`.
Grace expiry uses the next renewal, renewed-until or trial end (in that order),
excluding historical dates at/before cancellation, then a previously known valid
expiry. Conflicting usable trial and cycle deadlines raise `FluentError` rather
than guessing whether the subscription was on trial; the API omits that flag.
Equal instants are not conflicting, even with different timezone offsets.
`canceled_at` is the request time, never a grace deadline. If no deadline
is available, processing also raises `FluentError` and rolls back; monitor failures and
reconcile instead of assuming a new expiry. The prior committed state remains
until recovery, so hosts must apply their own stale-state entitlement policy.
Terminal cancellation uses `ended_at` or `canceled_at`; an active snapshot clears
stale expiry after a missed resume. Webhooks and Django reconciliation use the same
mapping. Core's internal `ends_at` is not currently exposed; `next_renewal_at` alone
must not be assumed universally present after cancellation.
`scheduled_update`, `has_scheduled_update`, and `cancellation_reason` read remotely.
`update_billing(body)` returns a hosted URL; both redirect defaults/overrides are required.

`model()` is local. `state()`/`subscription_state(ends_at, now)` implements PHP's
endsAt predicates: active/valid through grace period, recurring before cancellation,
ended at or beyond the end time. **Check Vatly status separately before granting
access**; these convenience predicates do not account for paused/unpaid states.

## Initial subscription linking

This alpha's linkage code reports `subscription_plan` lines as `legacy_plan_ids`.
It does not consume a related-resources subscription reference. Do not assume
an API addition alone completes this integration; package support must be
implemented and tested separately.

For existing subscription-valued lines, `await vatly.reconcile_checkout(checkout_id)` follows
host records → checkout → order → distinct subscription IDs, retries each 404 up
to three times (configurable 1–10), and returns `CheckoutResolution` with resolved
resources, `pending_subscription_ids`, and legacy IDs. Two lines for the same plan
can identify different subscriptions; quantity never multiplies IDs.

An unresolved subscription ID is not evidence of entitlement. Enqueue bounded
recovery and inspect ownership/status before granting access. The caller authorizes
the checkout and wraps local writes in its driver transaction. Built-in reactions
make no API reads. A future related-resources integration must preserve confirmed
IDs across older null snapshots and refresh unresolved signup correlation via GET;
core does not promise historical inference or backfill. Trial AUTH\_REQUEST flows
may have no merchant order.paid event; explicitly reconcile the paid checkout's orderId.


# Orders and reversals

`vatly.order(id).model()` lazily fetches one complete Order. `sync()` refreshes;
`lines()` shares the cached model; `invoice_url()` reads the invoice link.
`reversed_subtotal()`/`refundable_subtotal()` return exact `Decimal` currency-unit
amounts. `is_reversed`, `is_fully_reversed` and `is_partially_reversed` derive from
both totals. Do not use float arithmetic for money.

`refunds()` and `chargebacks()` read optional local repositories or return an empty
list. To mutate refunds or read any unsupported operation, use `vatly.api.orders`
and `vatly.api.refunds` directly. Signed reversal snapshots preserve taxes,
metadata, original-order references and mode. Their ownership follows the original
order's host checkout link; `entityType=order` does not make a chargeback an Order.


# Transactional webhooks

Call `await vatly.webhook_processor().handle(raw_bytes, signature_header)` in your
framework route. Signature/HMAC freshness checks happen before storage, using the
SDK. Missing/invalid signatures raise `VatlyInvalidSignatureError`. Keep the default
300-second tolerance; arrays of secrets support rotation. Unknown signed events
are retained and dispatched, not applied to known repositories.

Implement `WebhookCalls.process(event, work)` in **one transaction** shared by all
drivers. Lock/claim the signed event.id, skip committed duplicates, retain the
envelope, await work, mark processed and commit. Roll back every write on failure
so delivery retries can finish. Concurrency requires DB uniqueness/locking, not a
check-then-insert in memory. Scope every key by tenant/storefront/mode. An unsigned
Vatly-Event-Id header is not a dedup authority. Mode mismatches fail before storage.

| Event                                          | Built-in behavior                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| subscription.started                           | Upsert; newly saved row emits local.subscription\_created                             |
| subscription.updated / billing\_updated        | Update existing resource; null mandate preserves local value                          |
| subscription.resumed                           | Update existing row; clear ends\_at                                                   |
| cancellation / grace-period completion         | Update existing row and ends\_at                                                      |
| order.paid / payment\_failed                   | Upsert signed snapshot; new paid row emits local.order\_created                       |
| order.canceled                                 | Update existing snapshot only                                                         |
| refund.\* / order.chargeback\_\*               | Optional reversal upsert                                                              |
| checkout.paid                                  | Link own checkout record to order; link subscription IDs from an already stored order |
| scheduled updates / products / setup / unknown | Dispatch without built-in resource writes                                             |

Missing repositories skip persistence, not dispatch. Local-created events fire
only when a row is first saved, not on every payment status transition. Custom
`additional_webhook_reactions` run after built-ins and before final dispatch,
inside the same transaction. Write transactional outbox rows in `events.dispatch`,
then send external effects after commit. Throw on processing failure; respond 5xx,
not 2xx, so Vatly retries. A duplicate committed event may respond 200.

No implicit API reads occur. All six checkout/order/subscription delivery orders
are tested to converge using host records and stored snapshots. Missing snapshots,
AUTH\_REQUEST trials and legacy plan references need explicit reconciliation jobs.
Delayed stale events can still overwrite newer snapshots: dedup is not ordering;
reconcile conflicts with the API. Never infer ownership from customerId or metadata.


# Configuration and lifecycle

Construct `Vatly(Wiring(api=api, ...))` with an `AsyncVatlyClient`. The caller owns
the SDK connection pool: use `async with AsyncVatlyClient()` and reuse it per
application/worker lifespan. Fluent creates no additional transport. Pass an
explicit key or use `VATLY_API_KEY`. Live/test share the same URL; keys select mode.

Only `api` and both redirect URLs are needed for anonymous API-only checkout
creation. Add `checkouts` to persist `.for_entity(EntityRef(...))`; add repositories,
`webhook_secret`, `webhook_calls` and `events` for a durable integration. Missing
wiring fails when used. `api` exposes all SDK resources, options, retries and errors.

Use `RequestOptions` for stable idempotency keys, headers and timeouts (seconds).
SDK errors propagate unchanged. Keep API/webhook secrets server-side and separate.
An email-only profile does not create a customer. Authorization is always the host's job.

## Development and releases

Run `.agents/setup` to provision uv 0.12.9, Python 3.12, locked dependencies and an
import sanity check. It is idempotent, has no service/database/secret requirements,
and becomes active for project orbs after reaching the default branch.

uv retains a [pinned SDK wheel](https://github.com/vatly/vatly-fluent-python/blob/main/vendor/README.md){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} for reproducible development;
published metadata declares the exact PyPI dependency.
[`vatly-fluent-python` 0.1.0a2](https://pypi.org/project/vatly-fluent-python/0.1.0a2/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}
was published on 2026-11-12. Publish the matching SDK version first. Keep the
PyPI trusted publisher for project `vatly-fluent-python` with owner
`vatly`, repository `vatly-fluent-python`, workflow `release.yml`; leave the
environment field blank. No GitHub environment or API token is needed. Restrict
repository release access: there is no environment approval gate. Only publish a
GitHub release/tag after explicit authorization and green CI.
The tag must match `v` plus the package version. Pushing main does not publish.
PyPI artifacts are public even when the source GitHub repo is private.


# Driver contracts and ownership

Fluent's async `Protocol`s adapt existing databases; there are no framework models
or containers. Implement synchronous storage inside async adapters deliberately,
using your framework's thread/transaction rules. The [SQLite example](https://github.com/vatly/vatly-fluent-python/blob/main/examples/sqlite_driver.py){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}
demonstrates the contract, not a production async database strategy.

`Stored[T]` wraps the untouched SDK `resource` with `entity: EntityRef | None`.
`LocalSubscription` also adds `ends_at`. Repository methods are
`find_by_vatly_id`, `store` and `update`. `store` may return None to decline saving;
then no local-created event is emitted. `update` takes wrapper field changes:
omitted keys stay unchanged; None explicitly clears. `resource` is a complete SDK
snapshot. `ReversalRepository` adds `list_for_order` and `list_for_customer`.

Scope all unique IDs and lookups by tenant, storefront and test/live mode.
`CheckoutRecords.record(CheckoutRecord(...))` stores an authorized host entity.
`find(checkout_id)` reads it; `link(checkout_id, resource_type, resource_id)` binds
orders/subscriptions; `find_for_resource` follows the link. Identical repeats are
idempotent; conflicting ownership must fail, never silently reassign.

`CustomerBindings` is separate billing identity: atomic `bind`, non-clearing
`record`, and lookups in both directions. Unique constraints on both sides protect
concurrent binding. These bindings **never determine resource ownership**.

`WebhookCalls.process(event, work)` must commit signed-ID dedup, audit, repository
writes, checkout links and the outbox together. Write external effects to the outbox
with `EventDispatcher.dispatch`; send them after commit. Driver concurrency must
not interleave transactions on a shared connection. See [webhooks](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-python/webhooks).


# Customer portal

After authorizing the customer ID, call
`await vatly.customer(id).portal_session({"returnUrl": "https://app.example.com/billing"})`
using the production API's request fields. An empty `{}` body is also supported.
Redirect to `session.url`. It is short-lived/single-use; never log it or use it as
a permanent account URL. Errors propagate from the SDK without wrapping.

Do not accept arbitrary Vatly customer IDs from the browser. Look up the customer's
binding for the authenticated billable and tenant/storefront/mode first.
For subscription invoice-address updates, `subscription(local).update_billing()`
returns a hosted URL with success/cancellation redirects.


# Porting notes

See [PORTING.md](https://github.com/vatly/vatly-fluent-python/blob/main/PORTING.md){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} for upstream commits, API mapping, deliberate
Python differences, checkout/entity ownership, and subscription-linking compatibility.


# Testing

Run the README quality commands and `.agents/setup` twice for warm setup. Tests
use `httpx.MockTransport` through the real SDK; no remote mutations or fake parallel
API implementation. Static fixtures are synthesized from the SDK's pinned
production OpenAPI examples, not customer-account data.

The SQLite driver demonstrates persisted uniqueness, full snapshot storage,
mode/tenant scoping, immutable checkout links, deduplication, transaction rollback,
concurrent duplicate delivery and an outbox. It uses one connection/lock per driver
and is intentionally a small example, not a production multi-worker async adapter.

`test_helpers()` delegates test-only API mutations and includes `advance_renewal`,
`force_renewal_paid/failed` and `force_order_payment_paid/failed`. These helpers
change Vatly data. Use only with explicit test intent and a test key; the SDK
blocks live keys. CI and orb setup never use real credentials.


# Vatly Django guides

**Alpha — under active development. Every alpha release may include breaking changes. Pin exact versions during alpha.**

Pushes to `main` affecting `docs/**` notify `vatly/vatly-docs`, which imports
these guides automatically. The notifier requires the Actions secret
`VATLY_DOCS_DISPATCH_TOKEN` with Contents: write access to `vatly/vatly-docs`.

- [Configuration](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/django/configuration): settings, installation and authorized billables
- [Billing](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/django/billing): mixin, checkout, portal, subscription lifecycle
- [Storage and webhooks](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/django/webhooks): transactions, signed snapshots, outbox and recovery
- [Testing and release](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/django/development): supported versions, offline tests, boot and publishing


# Webhooks, storage and outbox

Register the configured HTTPS `billing/webhook/` path in Vatly separately. Setup
and CI never register endpoints or create remote test data. The route verifies raw
request bytes against Vatly-Signature (SDK HMAC, default ±300 seconds, secret rotation).
The signed event.id is the dedup key; untrusted event-ID headers are ignored.
Invalid signatures/payloads are 400, wrong methods405, committed duplicates200.
Processing failures propagate as 500 so Vatly retries; all local writes roll back.

Each scope+mode has a BillingScope row. An atomic UPDATE acquires its write lock
before dedup reads, serializing callbacks across workers. The same transaction
contains WebhookCall audit, immutable Checkout/ResourceLink writes, complete
BillingResource snapshots, processed\_at and Outbox rows. PostgreSQL is recommended
for concurrent production workers. SQLite supports local development; lock contention
may fail a delivery, which is safe to retry. Database uniqueness is the final guard.

Fluent's async protocols use thread-sensitive sync\_to\_async. ORMDriver.process
bridges the work callback with async\_to\_sync while the outer atomic transaction is
open, so nested writes remain on that same connection/thread. Never substitute
`thread_sensitive=False`, parallelize repository writes, or put network effects in
the callback. Storage assumes Django's default database; custom routers/multi-DB
transactions need a purpose-built driver. All models are scoped by tenant/storefront
and mode. Generic entity references deliberately have no cascading user deletion.
Handle GDPR retention/deletion explicitly through audited host administration.

Built-in reactions preserve signed snapshots and make no implicit API reads.
checkout.paid/order/subscription deliveries converge even when reordered. Only
subscription.started creates a missing local subscription; updates do not invent
one. Unknown events remain audited/dispatched. Optional refunds/chargebacks retain
full financial snapshots. Customer bindings are never an ownership fallback.
The alpha follows Fluent's last-delivery-wins snapshot semantics: dedup is not
event ordering; reconcile stale/conflicting events explicitly.

Outbox is durable, not an automatic sender. Implement a worker that claims rows
with database locks, sends using an idempotent consumer key (scope + outbox primary
key), and marks delivered\_at after success. Delivery is at least once, not exactly
once across external systems. Do not delete an outbox row before successful delivery.
Local-created notifications can precede eventual ownership linkage; consumers must
read current persisted ownership and retry/defer unattributed resources, not infer
it from customerId. No entitlements or email side effects are enabled by default.

Admin pages are read-only, but signed envelopes may contain personal data. Grant
model view permissions only to trusted staff and apply your retention policy.


# Billable operations

Render one server-generated UUID per purchase as a hidden `idempotency_key`. POST
to `billing/checkout/<offer>/` as an authenticated user with CSRF. Products, quantities,
customerId, metadata and redirect URLs come from server settings, not user input.
An invalid key/offer yields 400, a remote SDK error 502. Save/reuse the purchase key
when retrying ambiguous failures. A durable CheckoutAttempt commits before network
I/O and rejects key reuse for a different entity or changed payload. Never generate
a new key merely because payment creation timed out. Concurrent API retries use
the same key and local links are immutable/idempotent. Vatly's idempotency retention
still applies; investigate stale attempts instead of retrying them indefinitely.

The returned checkout URL redirects to Vatly. Success redirects do not prove payment.
Persisted Checkout records link order/subscription resources through signed events.
They never infer ownership from shared customer IDs or arbitrary metadata.

POST to `billing/portal/` to create a short-lived, single-use portal session for the
billable's bound customer. Do not cache/log the session URL. The portal request
uses the OpenAPI `returnUrl` field, not a query string or redirectUrl.

Mixin methods: `checkout`, `billing_portal`, `subscriptions`, `subscribed`,
`cancel_subscription`, `resume_subscription`, `swap_subscription`. Subscription
queries include only owned resources in the chosen scope/mode. `subscribed()`
requires active/trial/on\_grace\_period status and an unexpired local end time; it is
a convenience policy, not a replacement for your product's entitlement rules.
Grace expiry comes from Fluent's shared lifecycle mapping, not `canceledAt`
(the cancellation request time). Missing expiry raises `FluentError` and preserves
the prior committed state for explicit recovery; do not treat failed/stale syncs
as evidence of continuing entitlement. See Fluent's subscription guide for period
field precedence and the missing-deadline policy.
`Billing.subscription_action` also exposes sync, swap\_and\_invoice and
swap\_without\_charge. It checks local ownership before any API mutation. Cancellation
waits for signed events to update local state; resume refreshes immediately. Use
RequestOptions for stable mutation keys on the underlying Fluent/SDK when a workflow
must retry the same cancellation/swap. Never run these mutating methods on a GET.

`Billing.reconcile(billable, checkout_id)` checks own checkout ownership then fetches
checkout → order → subscriptions and persists snapshots/links transactionally.
It can hold the scope lock during bounded GET retries; run it in a background job
for busy deployments. It emits no local-created outbox event; consumers should
derive access from the reconciled records or implement their own durable policy.

## Initial subscription linking

Initial lines can be `subscription_plan` + plan ID.
There is no deterministic initial subscription ID to attach to a billable. The
result reports `legacy_plan_ids`; it never guesses by customerId/plan/quantity.
This alpha does not consume a related-resources subscription reference; any
new API reference needs a separately tested package update. Quantity does not
multiply subscription IDs, and identical plans can yield distinct subscriptions.
For existing subscription-valued lines, `pending_subscription_ids` records IDs
that could not be fetched, without granting access. Trial
AUTH\_REQUEST flows can lack order.paid; reconcile the paid checkout's orderId.
Historical lines are not backfilled. Do not claim a complete live initial
subscription-to-entity flow until core provides the reference or an explicit host
record establishes it. Renewal/update subscription lines remain usable.


# Configuration

Add `vatly_django` to INSTALLED\_APPS and run migrations. Include its URLs under
your billing prefix. Use Django auth/session/CSRF middleware for browser endpoints.
Use HTTPS in production; configure your reverse proxy, allowed hosts and CSRF origins
as usual. Never disable CSRF for checkout/portal. Only webhook is exempt.

| Setting                                  | Contract                                                                                    |
| ---------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| VATLY\_API\_KEY                          | Required; falls back to environment. test\_/live\_ chooses mode                             |
| VATLY\_SCOPE                             | Required stable tenant/storefront string (max 200 chars)                                    |
| VATLY\_WEBHOOK\_SECRET                   | Required for webhooks; string or rotation list, never client-side                           |
| VATLY\_REDIRECT\_URL\_SUCCESS / CANCELED | Required checkout HTTPS destinations                                                        |
| VATLY\_PORTAL\_REDIRECT\_URL             | Optional HTTPS returnUrl for hosted portal                                                  |
| VATLY\_CHECKOUTS                         | Server allowlist: offer slug → products, optional locale/metadata/billingAddress            |
| VATLY\_BILLABLE\_RESOLVER                | Optional dotted callable(request) → authorized saved Django model; defaults to request.user |
| VATLY\_SCOPE\_RESOLVER                   | Optional dotted callable(request) → tenant/storefront string, also used on webhook routes   |

For multi-tenant hosts, both resolvers must validate membership and select the
matching key and webhook secret through the deployment's settings strategy. Do not
trust query-string tenant IDs or webhook customerId to route ownership. The current
facade uses one API key/secret configuration per deployment; construct ORMDriver +
Fluent directly if you need a credential registry per tenant.

The abstract `vatly_django.mixins.BillableMixin` adds no columns; use it with a
custom user, team or organization model. Existing models need not inherit it:
`Billing(scope).checkout(model, offer, idempotency_key=uuid)` provides the same
behavior. Entity identities are model label + primary key (immutable across schema
renames unless you migrate billing references). The mixin's `billing()` can be
overridden to choose a trusted scope. Built-in views use explicit resolvers instead.

There is no automatic remote customer creation or email lookup. Call
`Billing.bind_customer(billable, authorized_customer_id)` from trusted provisioning
code to reuse a known customer. Binding uniqueness is enforced in both directions,
and does not assign entitlement ownership.


# Development, support and release

Python 3.10–3.14; Django 5.2 LTS, 6.0 and 6.1 within their Python compatibility ranges.
CI runs representative supported combinations plus PostgreSQL 17 concurrent delivery.
Tests use real ORM migrations + SDK MockTransport + signed local fixtures, no Vatly
account writes. They cover all event permutations, rollback including outbox/audit,
duplicate delivery, purchase-key recovery, authorization, CSRF, billing identity,
status/grace rules and legacy/new subscription references. The isolated built wheel
test migrates a fresh DB, imports the package, and checks py.typed.

`.agents/setup` provisions pinned uv 0.12.9 and Python 3.12, syncs the lockfile and
runs Django system checks. It is executable/idempotent and needs no secrets/services.
It does not migrate a host application's DB or seed data. `vendor/` pins unmodified
dependency wheels; compare SHA256SUMS when refreshing them.

[`vatly-django` 0.1.0a2](https://pypi.org/project/vatly-django/0.1.0a2/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} was published
on 2026-11-12; its import name is `vatly_django`. Keep the PyPI trusted publisher
owner `vatly`, repo `vatly-django`, workflow `release.yml`; leave the environment
field blank. No GitHub environment or PyPI token is needed. Restrict repository
release access: there is no environment approval gate. Publish SDK then Fluent
then Django. The release workflow builds/checks artifacts and only publishes on a
published GitHub release whose tag matches `v` plus the package version. No tag or
publication is triggered by pushing main. PyPI packages are public even if GitHub source is private.

> Official Vatly packages for your language or framework.

Vatly is the European merchant of record for AI, software and digital products. These official packages connect billing, subscriptions, and tax compliance to your application.
