These packages are in alpha. Every alpha release may include breaking changes. Pin exact versions during alpha. The Python packages require Python 3.10+ and are released at `0.1.0a2`; their import names are `vatly`, `vatly_fluent`, and `vatly_django`, respectively. For example, pin the SDK with `pip install vatly-api-python==0.1.0a2`.

PHP Fluent currently has two in-depth guides, not a complete getting-started section. Follow its [README](https://github.com/vatly/vatly-fluent-php#readme){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} for setup.

Not using one of these languages? You can use the [REST API directly](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/authentication) with any HTTP client.


# Lovable payments with Vatly

Use Vatly as the **European merchant of record for your Lovable app** to sell software, digital products, or SaaS subscriptions without building your own tax and invoicing workflow. Vatly is the European merchant of record for AI, software and digital products: it becomes the legal seller, while you build and deliver the product.

**[Get a test API key](https://my.vatly.com){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} · [Copy the Lovable agent prompt](https://docs.vatly.com/#prompt-lovable-to-build-the-integration)**

This is a custom API integration using Vatly's existing JavaScript packages, not a native Lovable payment connector or an endorsement by Lovable. You do not need a Vatly-specific change to Lovable or Vatly to follow this approach.

## Why use a merchant of record instead of plain Stripe?

Lovable can add a payment integration, but accepting a card payment is not the same as handing over the seller's responsibilities. With a standard payment-processing integration, your business remains the seller and must arrange tax compliance and invoicing. For a broader comparison, see [Vatly vs Stripe](https://vatly.com/vs/stripe){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

With Vatly, the [tax and invoicing for Vatly sales are Vatly's responsibility](https://vatly.com/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}: calculating and collecting EU VAT and applicable sales tax, handling registrations, filing and remitting tax, and issuing customer invoices. You still own your app, access control, and fulfillment. The difference is who takes on the legal seller's tax work, not just which checkout button you use.

## Why Vatly fits a Lovable app

- **Europe-first.** Vatly is based in the Netherlands and built for European software and digital product businesses selling internationally, with [European payment methods through Mollie](https://vatly.com/mollie-merchant-of-record){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.
- **Software billing, including AI apps.** Sell an AI app's subscription or a one-off digital product through the same [checkout API](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/checkouts). You do not need a payment integration specific to the model or AI service your app uses.
- **Multi-line orders.** A checkout can include multiple products and quantities, for example a subscription plan and a one-off digital download, with [order lines and tax information](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/orders) available to your backend.
- **Hosted checkout and customer portal.** Redirect customers to checkout instead of building a payment form. The [hosted portal](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/customerportal) provides invoice history and subscription controls for eligible customers; portal access requires an issued invoice.

## Start with a test checkout

**[Create your Vatly account](https://my.vatly.com){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}, get a test API key under Developers » API keys, and [copy the Lovable agent prompt](https://docs.vatly.com/#prompt-lovable-to-build-the-integration).** Create a test product under **Manage Products**, then let Lovable connect a checkout button to your existing backend using the prompt below. Enter the key only in Lovable's secure secret form, never in chat.

Test mode works from the start. Your first milestone is a hosted test checkout followed by a verified webhook that updates access in your app, not a complete billing UI built from scratch. Live sales require [Vatly approval, product review, and Mollie verification](https://docs.vatly.com/introduction#going-live). Product review typically takes one to two business days; that is not a guarantee of your integration or go-live date.

## Choose the right server code for your Lovable project

You keep your existing app, customer login, and database. Lovable adds a checkout action that sends customers to Vatly's hosted payment page, plus a background receiver for billing updates. After a verified payment, your app grants the purchased access. You do not need to build a card-entry form. For the responsibilities behind this flow, see [Build your own integration](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration).

Lovable's [current stack documentation](https://docs.lovable.dev/introduction/faq){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} distinguishes two kinds of app:

| Your project             | Where Vatly code belongs                                                                                                                                                   |
| ------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Newer TanStack Start app | A server function for authenticated checkout creation, and a public server route for signed webhooks. Keep SDK imports and secrets out of code shared with the browser.    |
| Older React + Vite app   | An Edge Function in Lovable's built-in backend (Lovable Cloud), or your connected Supabase project. A React component or Vite development server is not a private backend. |

Lovable says apps created from May 13, 2026 (June 22, 2026 for Enterprise workspaces) use TanStack Start. Inspect your actual project before choosing a route: an older project may have been upgraded. Its [direct API integration guide](https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/any-api){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} explains this server-function versus Edge Function split.

The [built-in backend](https://docs.lovable.dev/features/cloud){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} provides database, auth, storage, and Edge Functions using Supabase's open-source foundation. A [connected Supabase project](https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/supabase){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} gives you ownership of the backend in your own Supabase account. Use the backend you already have; adding Vatly does not require migrating it. Store user-to-Vatly-customer mappings and processed webhook IDs in your database.

## Add Vatly rather than the default payments flow

Lovable offers [built-in payments](https://docs.lovable.dev/features/payments){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} and other payment integrations. If you want **Vatly** to be the merchant of record, explicitly request a **direct Vatly API integration**. Do not ask only to "add payments": the agent could choose a different provider.

Lovable also supports [custom API connectors](https://docs.lovable.dev/integrations/any-api){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}. This guide uses server-side Vatly packages so your app owns checkout authorization, webhook verification, and fulfillment. It does not use Lovable's built-in payments setup or ask you to connect a Stripe account for Vatly.

The prompt below starts your agent with [`@getvatly/fluent`](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/readme), the higher-level JavaScript billing package. It provides building blocks for checkout, subscriptions, and webhook processing; your agent connects those to your database and access rules. The [general integration guide](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration#choose-your-tools) explains the alternatives, while the package docs own implementation examples.

## Set up the account and secrets

Follow the [Quickstart](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/quickstart), starting with a test key and product. Both `@getvatly/fluent` and its underlying `@getvatly/sdk` are **alpha**; use the compatible, exact versions in [fluent installation and configuration](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/configuration), because alpha updates may break compatibility.

When Lovable prompts for `VATLY_API_KEY`, use the secure **Add secret** form, not the chat. Manage project secrets under **More » Settings » Secrets**. If your app uses an external Supabase project, Lovable's **Manage secrets** opens the Supabase dashboard; store the secret in that project's Edge Function settings. See [Lovable secrets](https://docs.lovable.dev/features/secrets){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.

Add a separate `VATLY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` matching the signing secret configured for your Vatly webhook endpoint. Both values are **server-side only**. Never create `VITE_VATLY_API_KEY`, put the key in React code, or paste it into an agent prompt. Public Supabase connection values do not make a Vatly API key safe to expose.

## Prompt Lovable to build the integration

Paste this into Lovable after choosing your product and return URLs. Provide IDs and URLs when asked, but enter secret values only in the secure secret form.

```text
Use Vatly as the merchant of record for this app. Build a direct API
integration, not Lovable built-in payments or a Stripe/Paddle integration.

First inspect this project's framework and backend. If it uses TanStack
Start, keep checkout creation in a server function and webhooks in a public
server route. If it uses React + Vite, use an Edge Function in the existing
Lovable Cloud or connected Supabase backend. Do not migrate the backend.
Tell me which files and deployed routes will contain server-only code.

Read these sources before writing code:
https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration
https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/readme
https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/configuration
https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/checkouts
https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/webhooks
https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/coreconcepts
https://docs.vatly.com/guides/webhooks
https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference
https://docs.vatly.com/openapi.yaml

Start with @getvatly/fluent and its required @getvatly/sdk dependency.
Pin the compatible alpha versions documented in configuration and check
the deployed runtime; use pinned npm: imports for Deno. Use the underlying
SDK when a fluent helper is missing or the deployed runtime requires a
different approach, and explain the reason. Wire the documented storage
drivers to our database; do not assume adapters are included.
Ask me for a test-mode Vatly product ID and fixed success/canceled URLs.
Ask for VATLY_API_KEY and VATLY_WEBHOOK_SECRET through the secret form,
never chat. Never put either value in VITE_ variables or browser code.

Authenticate checkout requests, load or create the signed-in user's Vatly
customer on the server, and store the mapping in the database. Restrict
products and quantities server-side. Use the documented fluent checkout
or subscription builder and return only the hosted checkout URL to the
browser. Redirect there. Do not unlock access on return.

Make only the webhook route public without user JWT/session requirements.
Follow fluent's webhook guide: verify the untouched request with the
endpoint secret before writes, validate the envelope, and wire transactional
webhook storage. Reject bad signatures and acknowledge verified webhook.setup.
Use the verified event.id for deduplication; commit processing and database
changes atomically, with retries on failure. Configure access policies so users
cannot write their own billing/access state. Follow Vatly's actual event
names and envelope, and handle subscription cancellation and renewals.

Show me the deployed HTTPS webhook URL and which Vatly events to subscribe
to under Developers > Webhooks. Test auth, cross-user customer access, CORS
where needed, invalid signatures, duplicate events, and payment confirmation.
Report what you tested and what still needs my setup; do not claim live
payments work without a completed test-mode checkout and verified delivery.
```

Use the JavaScript packages in Lovable's managed server functions. A separately hosted backend can use [another package or the HTTP API](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration#choose-your-tools). If Lovable generates a Supabase function with JWT verification enabled for the webhook, ask it to allow external requests **only on that function**, while keeping Vatly signature verification mandatory. The checkout function must still require your user's authentication.

## Review the result in Lovable

- Ask the agent to identify the server-only SDK imports and show that the browser calls your backend, not `api.vatly.com` with your API key.
- In an older Vite app, confirm it deployed an Edge Function, not just a frontend helper. In a TanStack Start app, confirm the webhook is a deployed HTTP route, not a server function that only the UI can invoke.
- Confirm the return page stays pending until the database reflects a verified payment event, and database policies prevent clients from granting themselves access.
- Test unsigned, tampered, and stale webhooks, duplicate deliveries, and a database failure. Confirm retries cannot grant access twice. Follow [fluent testing](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/testing) and the [test-mode guide](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/testing).
- Register the deployed webhook URL in Vatly, not the editor preview URL. Do not replace the test key with a live key until [onboarding](https://docs.vatly.com/introduction#going-live) is complete.

Building in Bolt instead? See [Bolt payments with Vatly](https://docs.vatly.com/integrations/bolt).


# Bolt payments with Vatly

Add **Vatly payments to your Bolt.new app** without turning a generated checkout into a tax and invoicing project. Vatly is the European merchant of record for AI, software and digital products: it acts as the legal seller for your software, digital downloads, or subscriptions, while your Bolt app handles the product and customer access.

**[Sign up and get a test key](https://my.vatly.com){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} · [Copy the Bolt integration prompt](https://docs.vatly.com/#prompt-bolt-to-add-checkout-and-webhooks)**

This is a custom API integration, not a native Bolt connector or an endorsement by Bolt. It uses Vatly's existing API and JavaScript packages; no platform changes are required on Vatly's side.

## A payment integration is not a merchant of record

Bolt's Stripe integration can generate checkout and webhook code. With a standard payment-processing integration, though, your business is still the seller: you must arrange tax compliance and customer invoicing alongside the integration. The distinction is between processing a payment and taking on the seller's responsibilities. See [Vatly vs Stripe](https://vatly.com/vs/stripe){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} for the broader comparison.

Vatly takes on the latter for Vatly sales. It handles [EU VAT, applicable sales tax, registrations, returns, remittance, and customer invoices](https://vatly.com/){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}. That leaves Bolt's server functions responsible for a smaller integration: create checkout, verify billing events, and update your app's access state. Your product logic and fulfillment remain yours.

## What Vatly gives your Bolt app

- **A European merchant of record.** Vatly is based in the Netherlands and focuses on European software and digital products, with [Mollie-powered European payment methods](https://vatly.com/mollie-merchant-of-record){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} for international sales.
- **A fit for AI and software products.** Sell access to an AI tool or SaaS app as a subscription, or sell a one-off license or digital download. Use Vatly's existing API rather than building a billing system around your frontend framework.
- **One checkout, multiple order lines.** Pass products and quantities to the [checkout API](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/checkouts), then use the resulting [order lines](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference/orders) to fulfill a purchase containing more than one item.
- **Hosted billing screens.** Vatly provides the checkout and a [customer portal](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/customerportal) for invoices and subscription management. Portal access requires an issued invoice; you still authenticate the user and create the portal session on your server.

## Get your first test payment working

**[Sign up for Vatly](https://my.vatly.com){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}, get a test API key under Developers » API keys, and [copy the Bolt integration prompt](https://docs.vatly.com/#prompt-bolt-to-add-checkout-and-webhooks).** Add a test product in **Manage Products**. Bolt can then build the server functions and checkout button against your existing Bolt Database or Supabase backend; you do not need to switch database providers to use Vatly.

Start in test mode as soon as your account is ready, with credentials stored in database **Secrets**. Verify a complete test checkout and webhook before considering the integration ready. Going live also depends on [Vatly approval, product review, and Mollie business verification](https://docs.vatly.com/introduction#going-live). Product review typically takes one to two business days, but neither that nor generated code guarantees a launch date.

## Identify your Bolt backend first

Your customers keep using your Bolt app. A checkout button sends them to Vatly's hosted payment page, and a background billing update tells your app when to grant access. You keep the product UI, login, and database; Vatly handles checkout, tax, and invoicing. See [Build your own integration](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration) for the overall responsibilities before asking the agent to make changes.

Bolt supports [JavaScript frontend frameworks and Node.js backends](https://support.bolt.new/reference/supported-technologies){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}, rather than requiring one frontend framework. Inspect `package.json` and the deployed backend instead of assuming every app is a React + Vite app or that a Node process in the editor is deployed as a production server.

New projects use [Bolt Database by default](https://support.bolt.new/integrations/supabase){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}. Bolt Cloud [server functions](https://support.bolt.new/bolt-cloud/database/server-functions){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}, also called edge functions, handle external API calls, payments, and webhooks outside the browser. They belong to the connected database, and Bolt deploys them when it creates or updates them.

You can also use an existing Supabase project with its database, authentication, and Edge Functions. Bolt's Supabase integration is available on Pro and Teams plans. Keep the database your app already uses: replacing its connection can risk existing data, and Vatly does not require a database migration to another provider.

| Existing setup                    | Where to add Vatly                                                                                                                     |
| --------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Bolt Cloud with Bolt Database     | Server functions for authenticated checkout creation and a separate signed webhook endpoint.                                           |
| Connected Supabase project        | Supabase Edge Functions and the existing auth/database integration.                                                                    |
| Separately hosted Node.js backend | Private server routes and that host's runtime secrets. Confirm the routes actually deploy; a browser-only static host cannot run them. |

This guide focuses on Bolt Cloud and Supabase. For a separately hosted backend, choose a [package or direct HTTP integration](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration#choose-your-tools) that fits its runtime.

## Use Vatly, not Bolt's Stripe integration

Bolt's [built-in Stripe integration](https://support.bolt.new/integrations/stripe){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"} imports Stripe products and generates checkout and webhook code. Those conveniences apply to Stripe, **not to a custom Vatly integration**. Do not paste a Vatly key into the Stripe setup or reuse Stripe event names, signatures, or test cards.

Tell the agent to use Vatly explicitly. Create your products in Vatly, create checkouts on your server, and register your webhook URL in Vatly yourself. Your app remains responsible for authorizing checkout requests and updating access from verified Vatly events.

The prompt below starts your agent with [`@getvatly/fluent`](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/readme), the higher-level JavaScript billing package. Your agent connects its checkout and webhook building blocks to your existing database and access rules; it is not a ready-made Bolt Database or Supabase adapter. For other approaches, see [Choose your tools](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration#choose-your-tools). Implementation examples live in the package docs.

## Configure the database and secrets

1. Follow the [Quickstart](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/quickstart) to get a test key and product ID.
2. Ensure your Bolt project has a connected database. Bolt's server functions and secrets require one; if none exists, ask the agent to add it before building the payment functions.
3. Open the **database icon » Secrets** and add `VATLY_API_KEY` using your Vatly `test_` key. Add `VATLY_WEBHOOK_SECRET` with the signing secret configured for your Vatly webhook endpoint. Bolt can also prompt you to add these securely. See [Bolt secrets](https://support.bolt.new/bolt-cloud/database/secrets){rel="&#x22;nofollow&#x22;"}.
4. Use **database icon » Server Functions** to inspect the generated functions and their logs. Never log the keys or full billing payloads while debugging.

Secrets are available to server functions, not browser code. Do not put Vatly credentials in Bolt's project `.env`, `VITE_*` variables, frontend components, or agent chat. With a separately hosted backend, configure equivalent private runtime secrets on that host.

Both `@getvatly/fluent` and its underlying `@getvatly/sdk` are **alpha**. Use the compatible, exact versions in [fluent installation and configuration](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/configuration) and review breaking changes before upgrading.

## Prompt Bolt to add checkout and webhooks

Use this prompt in your Bolt project. The agent should ask for product IDs and app URLs, not for secret values in chat.

```text
Integrate Vatly as this app's merchant of record for payments and billing.
Do not use Bolt's Stripe integration, Stripe products, or Stripe webhooks.

Inspect package.json and identify the deployed backend. Keep the current
Bolt Database or Supabase connection; do not replace it. If there is no
database, explain that Bolt server functions and secrets need one and set
it up before adding the functions. Use deployed server functions for
checkout creation and a separate public Vatly webhook receiver, not a
browser-only helper or a Node server that only runs in the editor.

Read:
https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration
https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/readme
https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/configuration
https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/checkouts
https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/webhooks
https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/coreconcepts
https://docs.vatly.com/guides/webhooks
https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference
https://docs.vatly.com/openapi.yaml

Start with @getvatly/fluent and its required @getvatly/sdk dependency.
Pin the compatible alpha versions documented in configuration and check
the deployed runtime; use pinned npm: imports for Deno. Use the underlying
SDK when a fluent helper is missing or the deployed runtime requires a
different approach, and explain the reason. Wire the documented storage
drivers to our database; do not assume adapters are included. Ask me to add
VATLY_API_KEY and VATLY_WEBHOOK_SECRET via database Secrets, never in chat
or .env. Keep SDK imports and credentials exclusively in server functions.
Ask me for a test-mode product ID and fixed success/canceled return URLs.

Require authentication for checkout creation. Load or create the Vatly
customer for the signed-in user and keep a server-owned database mapping.
Never accept an arbitrary customer ID, price, or redirect URL from the UI.
Allowlist products and validate quantities server-side. Use the documented
fluent checkout or subscription builder; return only its hosted checkout
URL so the browser can redirect. Add CORS handling restricted to
my app's origins where functions are cross-origin. A return URL visit must
never grant access.

The webhook function must accept Vatly without a user JWT, while checkout
creation stays authenticated. Follow fluent's webhook guide: verify the
untouched request with the endpoint secret before writes, validate the
envelope, and wire transactional webhook storage. Reject invalid signatures
and acknowledge verified webhook.setup. Use the signed event.id for
deduplication, commit processing and database changes atomically, and retry
on failure. Protect billing tables from client writes.
Implement Vatly event names and top-level object payloads, including the
subscription lifecycle when selling subscriptions, not data.object.

Show the deployed functions and HTTPS webhook URL, the Vatly events I need
to subscribe to, and where to inspect function logs. Test login enforcement,
cross-user isolation, invalid signatures, duplicate/concurrent deliveries,
storage failure retries, and a completed test checkout. Distinguish tested
behavior from configuration or deployment work I still need to do.
```

Use the JavaScript packages in Bolt's managed server functions. A separately hosted backend can use [another package or the HTTP API](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration#choose-your-tools). For Supabase Edge Functions, Vatly's webhook route needs JWT verification disabled for that function only: Vatly's signature, not a user's session, authenticates deliveries.

## Debug a deployed Bolt integration

| Symptom                                            | What to check                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| -------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No Secrets or Server Functions view                | A database must be connected. Ask Bolt to confirm which backend it uses before creating another one.                                                                                                  |
| Checkout works in preview but not after publishing | Confirm the function deployed, the runtime has its secret, and CORS allows the published app's origin. The frontend preview alone does not prove a working backend.                                   |
| Vatly cannot register or deliver to the webhook    | Use the deployed public HTTPS function URL. Remove user-JWT requirements from that endpoint only, verify Vatly signatures, and acknowledge signed `webhook.setup`.                                    |
| Webhook reports an invalid signature               | Confirm the matching endpoint secret and verify the raw body before any JSON parsing. Use Vatly's verifier, not Stripe's.                                                                             |
| User pays but access stays pending                 | Inspect Server Functions logs and the durable inbox. Check event subscriptions, test/live mode, customer mapping, and failed database transactions. Do not bypass verification to make access appear. |

Follow [fluent testing](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/fluent-js/testing) and the [test-mode guide](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/testing) before publishing for customers. Confirm unsigned, tampered, and stale webhooks are rejected, concurrent duplicates cannot fulfill twice, and storage failures can retry. Complete [Vatly onboarding](https://docs.vatly.com/introduction#going-live) before switching to live credentials.

Building in Lovable instead? See [Lovable payments with Vatly](https://docs.vatly.com/integrations/lovable).


# Integrations

Connect Vatly to the tools and platforms you use to build your app. Vatly is the European merchant of record for AI, software and digital products, handling tax and customer invoicing while your app delivers the product.

[]{#choose-your-builder}

## Find your platform

| Platform                                               | How to get started                                                                                                           |
| ------------------------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Lovable](https://docs.vatly.com/integrations/lovable) | Understand how Vatly fits your Lovable app, prepare the account and secrets, and give Lovable's agent the integration brief. |
| [Bolt.new](https://docs.vatly.com/integrations/bolt)   | Connect Vatly to your existing Bolt app and backend, then have the agent build and test your checkout and billing flow.      |

The Lovable and Bolt guides describe custom integrations using Vatly's existing packages and API. They are not native payment connectors or endorsements by those platforms.

[]{#choose-your-integration-approach}[]{#create-a-checkout-with-the-javascript-sdk}[]{#create-a-checkout}[]{#prepare-your-vatly-account}[]{#keep-credentials-on-the-server}[]{#verify-webhooks-before-granting-access}[]{#before-you-connect}[]{#test-before-publishing}[]{#documentation-for-your-agent}

## Framework packages

Using a framework rather than an app builder? Official [Laravel](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/laravel/readme) and [Django](https://docs.vatly.com/packages/django/readme) packages integrate Vatly with your application. Their installation, configuration and API guides live under [Packages](https://docs.vatly.com/packages), alongside the SDKs and fluent packages, rather than being duplicated here.

These packages are in alpha. Every alpha release may include breaking changes. Pin exact versions during alpha.

## Connecting another app?

Start with [Build your own integration](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/build-your-own-integration) to understand what Vatly handles, what your app needs, and what to ask your developer or agent to build. It also helps you choose a fluent package, SDK, or direct API approach.

If you are ready for your first API request, follow the [Quickstart](https://docs.vatly.com/guides/quickstart). Implementation examples live in the [package docs](https://docs.vatly.com/packages), with exact endpoint and field details in the [API reference](https://docs.vatly.com/api-reference).
